valueProposition: Spacecraft engineering doesn't leave room for "close enough" — a control system that's 95% correct is a control system that fails, and a design review won't let a bug ship because it's rare. That standard carries over directly: the same intolerance for untested edge cases and unhandled failure states shows up in every commercial asset I ship.

Coursework in spacecraft design, orbital mechanics, and controls theory builds systems-thinking as a default habit — modeling how one component's failure propagates through the rest, instrumenting things so problems are diagnosable instead of mysterious, and validating a design before committing to it. That's the same instinct behind a multiplayer building system that replicates cleanly instead of desyncing under load.
It also means being fluent in the math and physics most software work never touches — genuinely useful when a gameplay system needs real simulation instead of an approximation.
